claims.text: Schwab states in its 2025 10-K that, as one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., its scale lets it spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients.

Schwab states in its 2025 10-K that its operating efficiency, coupled with scale and shared infrastructure across businesses, creates a cost advantage enabling competitive pricing while profitably serving clients across channels.
On the 4Q25 earnings call, Schwab said its sheer scale combined with efficiency efforts keeps its cost-to-serve clients low, allowing it to invest in client capabilities that fuel growth.
On the 4Q25 earnings call, Schwab said its scale combined with expense discipline decreased its cost per account 20% over the last five years.

On the 1Q25 earnings call, Schwab said its marketing spend drives approximately 40% of new-to-firm retail clients, and its investor-day deck states its data and insight-led marketing model drives efficiency at scale.
In its 3Q26 deck, Schwab states that 90% of accounts are opened digitally and that it leverages its scale to maintain a structural cost advantage while continuing to invest in growth.
In its 2026 investor-day deck, Schwab cites multiple growth levers across its leading platform for winning new clients across Retail, Advisor Services, and Workplace channels.
On the 1Q25 earnings call, Schwab cited its transfer of assets ratio of 1.5, meaning for every dollar that leaves Schwab, $1.50 comes from competitors.
On the 4Q25 earnings call, Schwab stated that in 2025 about half of new-to-firm retail clients initiated access to its thinkorswim trading platform.
On the 1Q26 earnings call, CEO Rick Wurster cited Schwab's massive scale, data and technological prowess, saying AI opens up new distribution channels for growth.

Schwab defines core net new client assets in its 2025 10-K as net new client assets before significant one-time inflows or outflows (generally greater than $25 billion) and activity from off-platform brokered CDs.
For full-year 2024, Schwab reported core net new assets of $366.9 billion (up 20% from 2023) and 4.2 million new brokerage accounts (up 10% year-over-year).
For full-year 2025, Schwab reported core net new assets of $519.4 billion (up 42% from 2024) and 4.7 million new brokerage accounts (up 13% from 2024).
In the first quarter of 2026, Schwab reported core net new assets of $140.0 billion (up 2% year-over-year) and 1.3 million new brokerage accounts (up 10%).
In the second quarter of 2026, Schwab reported core net new assets of $119.8 billion (up 49% year-over-year) and 1.4 million new brokerage accounts (up 26%).

On the 3Q26 earnings call, Schwab reported that clients opened 1.2 million brokerage accounts in the third quarter of 2026 and that it attracted $190 billion in core net new assets, up 38% over the prior year.

In its 2025 10-K, Edward Jones states its branch office model serves clients through deep, personal relationships and comprehensive advice and planning with financial advisors located in the communities where clients live and work.
In its 2025 10-K, Edward Jones states it targets new clients through High Net Worth, Workplace, and a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors.

Trade press reports that Edward Jones advisors leverage the firm's local footprint to prospect and win workplace retirement plans, with a technology platform (leveraging Aboon Workplace) covering the full plan lifecycle from prospecting to servicing.
In its 2025 10-K, Edward Jones reports operating expenses increased 11% to $15,610 million in 2025, and income before allocations of $2,090 million with a margin of 11.7%.
In its 2025 10-K, Edward Jones reports financial advisor compensation and benefits expense increased 12% to $6,969 million in 2025, and variable compensation increased 11% to $2,710 million.
In its 2025 10-K, Edward Jones reports communications and data processing expense increased 16% to $1,162 million in 2025 due to investments in new tools and technology.
In its 1Q26 10-Q, Edward Jones reports advertising expense of $43 million in the first quarter of 2026, compared with $39 million in the first quarter of 2025.

In its 2025 10-K, Edward Jones states its strategic ambition includes continuing to invest in technology to scale its ability to provide financial planning and to attract and serve new client segments.

Trade press reports Edward Jones has taken a minority stake in the personal finance app Quicken, with the stated intention of integrating Quicken's capabilities into Edward Jones, though the firm says it is still determining the deployment strategy.

Whether Edward Jones could replicate Schwab's scale-based low-cost client acquisition strategy cannot be assessed on this evidence, because Schwab's cited materials contain no statement about Edward Jones replicating its approach, and Edward Jones's cited materials describe its own branch-based model and technology initiatives rather than any adoption of Schwab's scale model.
